cards.a: The control plane (vManage/vSmart), the data plane (transport tunnels), and policy. Failures are control connections down, TLOC issues, or policy dropping traffic.

cards.q: What are the SD-WAN architecture components and their roles?
cards.a: vManage (admin UI), vSmart (control policy), vBond (orchestration), vEdge/cEdge (data plane), and vAnalytics (reporting).

cards.q: What is the first SD-WAN check?
cards.a: show sdwan control connections, which shows connectivity to vSmart and vBond. Control connections must be up before data works.

cards.q: What commands show the SD-WAN data plane?
cards.a: show sdwan tunnel (data tunnels) and show sdwan interface (transport).

cards.q: What is the SD-WAN troubleshooting order?
cards.a: Control plane first, then tunnels, then policy. Control plane must be up before data tunnels work.

cards.q: What does a tunnel down in SD-WAN indicate?
cards.a: A TLOC (transport locator) issue with the transport interface.

cards.q: What drives SD-WAN path selection and failover?
cards.a: BFD/SLA measurements, which determine the health of transport paths and drive path selection.

cards.q: What port does SD-WAN use for DTLS control connections?
cards.a: DTLS port 12346 for control plane connectivity.

cards.q: When policy drops traffic silently in SD-WAN, what should you check?
cards.a: The policy match (data-prefix or application) and action, since a wrong match or action causes traffic to be dropped.

cards.q: What is the difference between centralized and localized SD-WAN policy?
cards.a: Centralized policy is applied by vSmart for control and data plane; localized policy applies to interfaces.

cards.q: A vSmart with no connection to the vEdge is most likely caused by what?
cards.a: A certificate or reachability problem preventing the control connection from forming.

cards.q: What command shows BFD sessions for SLA health?
A vBond that is unreachable is most likely caused by what?
cards.a: A DNS/IP problem resolving and reaching the vBond orchestration node.
